headline: SSR MINING DROPS C$712M ON ROXMORE'S CONVERSE GOLD — 5.57Moz AU ADJACENT TO MARIGOLD AT 27% PREMIUM
snippet: SSR Mining (NASDAQ: SSRM) agreed to acquire Roxmore Resources (TSX: RM) in an all-cash deal valued at approximately C$712 million, offering C$6.75 per share — a 27% premium over Roxmore's October 9 closing price. The deal delivers SSR the Converse Gold Project in Nevada, which hosts 5.57Moz Au in Measured and Indicated resources and sits just 6km west of SSR's Marigold mine, potentially adding 150,000–170,000 ounces of annual production over 10+ years. Roxmore's remaining exploration assets (Rattlesnake Hills, Newton, Shabu River) transfer to a spinout company in which SSR will retain a 14.99% stake — an embedded optionality play for investors watching the deal.

headline: TOP 50 MINERS SHED $264 BILLION AS GOLD TRADE UNWINDS AND LITHIUM EXITS — BROAD MARKET CAP DESTRUCTION ACROSS SECTOR
snippet: Mining.com's Q3 2026 analysis of the world's 50 largest mining companies shows a combined market cap loss of US$264 billion as two powerful forces converged: gold's correction from January's $5,589 per ounce peak and a synchronized exit from lithium equities on oversupply fears. The dual selloff is notable for its breadth — producers across gold, silver and battery metals all fell together, a pattern that typically signals institutional repositioning rather than company-specific risk. The analysis provides useful context for junior investors: when sector-wide pressure eases, small-cap explorers historically lead the recovery in a leveraged bounce.

headline: CENTAURI MINERALS DRILLS RIO GRANDE FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2013 — 24,000M PHASE 1 TARGETS GOLD-COPPER SYSTEM
snippet: Centauri Minerals announced October 13 that it has mobilized a drill rig at its Rio Grande gold-copper project for the first time since 2013 — a 13-year gap that leaves a fully-funded Phase 1 program as a genuine exploration catalyst. The Phase 1 program covers approximately 24,000 metres and is expected to take six months into Q2 2027; management noted that earlier work confirmed gold-copper mineralization but was limited in scope. Drill results from Phase 1 will be the first material news flow from this project in over a decade, making it a genuine watch-list candidate for junior exploration investors.

headline: USA RARE EARTH, MP MATERIALS BOTH DROP 6% — VanEck REMX ETF -5% AS SECTOR SELLOFF DEEPENS
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) and MP Materials (MP) each fell approximately 6% on October 12, dragging the VanEck Rare Earth & Strategic Metals ETF (REMX) down roughly 5% — its worst single-session decline in weeks — while the S&P 500 was near flat. 24/7 Wall St. flags a specific risk for USAR: the company's government funding is tied to meeting future milestones rather than being drawn immediately, creating uncertainty about the timing and sufficiency of federal support. The selloff underscores that the rare earth trade is not just a China tension proxy — execution risk at individual companies matters, even with strategic tailwinds.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,165 AND SILVER $60.43 AS US DOLLAR HITS 18-MONTH HIGH — PRECIOUS METALS AWAIT US CPI DATA
snippet: Spot gold traded in a narrow range near $4,165–$4,182 per ounce on October 13 while silver fell to approximately $60.43, with both metals under headwinds from a US dollar that touched an 18-month high as investors positioned ahead of upcoming Consumer Price Index data. The gold-silver ratio sits at roughly 69:1 — elevated versus its long-run mean near 60 — suggesting silver continues to lag bullion in the current correction from the January $5,589 gold peak. A hot CPI print could extend the dollar's run and push both metals lower; a miss could reignite the precious metals trade for junior producers and royalty companies.

headline: KAZATOMPROM TQZ ACID PLANT NOW SLIPPING TO 2027-28 — WORLD'S LARGEST URANIUM PRODUCER FACES MULTI-YEAR SUPPLY GAP
snippet: Kazatomprom's TQZ sulfuric acid plant in Turkestan Province — designed for 800,000 tonnes per year of capacity critical to in-situ recovery leaching — has slipped further behind schedule, with completion now expected between Q3 2027 and Q1 2028 after a paleontological discovery delayed earthworks. The delay compounds existing Russian acid import restrictions and rising procurement costs, and while Kazatomprom reiterated its 2026 guidance of 27,500–29,000 metric tonnes, the supply constraint feeds directly into 2027 and 2028 models that many uranium bulls have not yet priced in. Long-term contract prices remain near an 18-year high above $96.50/lb — the equity-price disconnect for producers is narrowing.

headline: URANIUM SPECULATORS ARE LOADING UP: BENZINGA FLAGS POSITIONING SHIFT AHEAD OF UTILITY RE-CONTRACTING SEASON
snippet: Benzinga's October 2026 analysis argues that uranium is entering a speculative positioning phase distinct from the 2023-2024 spot squeeze, as utility re-contracting accelerates and the forward supply picture tightens with Kazatomprom production headwinds. The piece dubs uranium 'the other yellow metal' and profiles why fund managers are adding uranium exposure as a hedge against both energy-security risk and dollar weakness — even as listed producers like Paladin and Deep Yellow have underperformed spot in recent weeks, creating what bulls call an entry window. For junior uranium developers, the speculative bid at the commodity level is a necessary precursor to equity re-rating.

headline: VICTORY BATTERY METALS PIVOTS INTO URANIUM — FOUR QUEBEC CLAIM GROUPS ACQUIRED FROM GLOBEX MINING
snippet: Victory Battery Metals (TSX-V) announced it has acquired four uranium claim groups in Quebec Province from Globex Mining Enterprises, expanding its critical minerals portfolio from battery metals into uranium in a deal that reflects the breadth of capital now flowing into the Canadian uranium junior space. The Quebec claims are early-stage but sit in a jurisdiction with established uranium exploration history. The diversification move signals that even companies built around EV battery metals are pivoting toward nuclear fuel as uranium's long-term contract pricing holds near 18-year highs.

headline: STOCKHOUSE PROFILES RARE EARTHS AMERICAS AND LEADING EDGE MATERIALS AS WESTERN ANSWERS TO CHINA'S REE LOCK ON SUPPLY
snippet: A Stockhouse analysis dated October 13 profiles Rare Earths Americas and Leading Edge Materials (TSX-V: LEM) as among the most credible non-Chinese rare earth developers in the Western Hemisphere, citing a long-term market opportunity expected to add more than US$30 billion in value through 2034. The piece argues both companies are positioned to benefit from the structural de-risking of Western supply chains from China — a theme that has driven deal flow from Lynas in Brazil to AuKing in Greenland — and highlights that today's selloff in US-listed REE names (USAR, MP) contrasts sharply with underlying demand fundamentals for NdPr and other critical rare earths.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE TOPS OCTOBER SCREEN: ANALYSTS FAVOR LOW-COST PRODUCERS AS GOLD CORRECTS 25% FROM $5,589 PEAK
snippet: Yahoo Finance's October 2026 screen of gold equities highlights Agnico Eagle Mines (AEM) at the top of its shortlist for investors navigating the gold price correction from January's $5,589 high to current levels near $4,165. The analysis emphasizes that Agnico's industry-leading cost structure and tier-one Canadian asset base give it margin resilience that most mid-tier producers lack at current realized prices. The piece reinforces a theme emerging across October commentary: with gold miners falling 2-5x harder than spot in the correction, operational leverage cuts both ways — low-cost producers become the defensive play while high-cost operators face existential pressure.
